extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and counsel in reciprocal-discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for imposing reciprocal discipline on practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including the mandatory nature of reciprocal discipline, the Selling v. Radford review factors, burdens of proof, and when discipline may be served nunc pro tunc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory nature of reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director 'shall' impose reciprocal discipline (public censure, public reprimand, probation, disbarment, suspension, or disciplinary disqualification) predicated upon state-level public discipline unless the practitioner clearly and convincingly demonstrates a genuine issue of material fact as to specified Selling factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.24 sets a streamlined, mandatory process: upon notification of state discipline the OED Director 'shall' obtain the certified record, file a complaint complying with § 11.34, and request the USPTO Director to issue notice; the USPTO Director then 'shall' consider any timely response and impose identical discipline unless one of the Selling factors is shown. The Order emphasizes the regulatory 'shall' language and related case law indicating lack of discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling v. Radford review factors (codified in § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be avoided only if the respondent clearly and convincingly demonstrates a genuine issue of material fact that: (i) the procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process; (ii) there was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct that the Office could not accept the conclusion as final; (iii) imposition of the same discipline by the Office would result in a grave injustice; or (iv) an argument that the practitioner was not publicly censured, publicly reprimanded, placed on probation, disbarred, suspended or disciplinarily disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Selling factor is a discrete basis to oppose reciprocal discipline; the respondent bears the burden to prove, by clear and convincing evidence, a genuine issue of material fact as to any one of these elements. Courts have treated these factors narrowly; USPTO mirrors that approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden of proof — clear and convincing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner must demonstrate by clear and convincing evidence that there is a genuine issue of material fact as to one of the Selling factors to avoid imposition of identical reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal precedent and the Order stress that this is a demanding standard and that the USPTO Director is not sitting as a court of review to relitigate state findings; the burden is on the respondent in reciprocal discipline cases (citing In re Kramer, In re Friedman, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner notification requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner is required to notify the OED Director in writing within 30 days of being disciplined in another jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification triggers the OED Director's obligations under § 11.24 to obtain certified records and initiate reciprocal-discipline proceedings. Failure to notify promptly can affect eligibility for certain relief (e.g., nunc pro tunc treatment).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's procedural duties upon receiving notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving notice of state discipline, the OED Director 'shall' obtain a certified copy of the record or order; 'shall' file with the USPTO Director a complaint complying with § 11.34 predicated on the state discipline; and 'shall' request the USPTO Director to issue notice to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order illustrates these duties in practice (OED filed a Request for Notice and Order and a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline). The OED Director may initially request a particular reciprocal sanction based on available records and adjust the requested discipline if later-cited facts (e.g., early termination of state probation) come to light.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director's hearing and decision-making process under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director 'shall' hear the matter on the documentary record unless the Director determines a hearing is necessary and 'shall' consider any timely filed response from the practitioner in deciding whether to impose identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director examines the record for Selling-factor issues; the proceeding is typically documentary and not a full de novo review of state proceedings. The Order demonstrates issuance of a Notice and Order and a schedule for briefs (e.g., Respondent given an opportunity to respond; briefing sequence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'shall' — limited agency discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory use of the command 'shall' in § 11.24 indicates mandatory, non-discretionary obligations on the OED Director and USPTO Director to pursue and impose reciprocal discipline except as the regulation itself allows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites case law (e.g., Natural Resources Defense Council; Lopez) interpreting 'shall' as a lack of discretion and relies on judicial precedent applying § 11.24 to conclude reciprocal discipline is mandatory unless Selling factors are met. Arguments that the agency has broad 'common sense' discretion to deviate from identical reciprocal discipline are rejected absent regulatory exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and standard for imposition of reciprocal discipline nunc pro tunc (§ 11.24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for imposition of reciprocal discipline nunc pro tunc, the respondent must (1) have promptly notified the OED Director of the discipline imposed by the other jurisdiction and (2) establish by clear and convincing evidence that he voluntarily ceased all activities related to practice before the Office and complied with all provisions of § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nunc pro tunc (concurrent) service of reciprocal discipline is not automatic; the practitioner must show prompt notice and an actual cessation of practice before the USPTO and compliance with § 11.58. The Order notes that voluntary cessation must be proven by clear and convincing evidence and that the USPTO's requirement to cease practice cannot be waived without extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary waiver authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any regulatory requirement may be suspended or waived by the USPTO Director 'in an extraordinary situation, when justice requires' upon petition by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states no petition invoking § 11.3 was raised and that no extraordinary circumstances were identified to justify suspending the mandatory provisions of § 11.24; invoking § 11.3 is therefore a narrow and exceptional route to relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of reciprocal discipline and public notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline serves to prevent a lawyer admitted in multiple jurisdictions from avoiding discipline by practicing elsewhere and to protect the public and the administration of justice; reprimands are public discipline and the OED Director must publish notice (e.g., Official Gazette) and notify state disciplinary agencies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and the public pursuant to § 11.59 and related rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order stresses the remedial and protective purposes of public discipline (citing ABA Standards and prior USPTO decisions). Reprimands are listed as tools available to the OED Director (§ 11.20(a)); the Director is ordered to publish a Notice of Discipline in the Official Gazette and provide notice to relevant agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave injustice analysis — whether sanction 'fits' the misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that imposition of identical reciprocal discipline would result in a 'grave injustice' is evaluated by asking whether the severity of punishment fits the misconduct; if the state discipline was within the appropriate range of sanctions for the misconduct, reciprocal discipline ordinarily is not a grave injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites case law (e.g., In re Thav; In re Kramer; In re Benjamin) and explains that mitigation arguments must show the state sanction was so ill-fitted that imposing the same discipline would be unjust. The practitioner's admission that state sanction was within the appropriate range undercuts a grave-injustice claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation detail — proof of completion of CLE and non-duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will consider proof of successful completion of CLE required by a state discipline when imposing reciprocal probation and will not require the practitioner to retake an identical CLE already completed during the corresponding state-imposed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order clarifies that the OED Director would accept evidence that the practitioner completed the CLE during the state probation and that the Agency will not impose duplicative CLE requirements; this is an implementation detail to ensure reciprocal discipline mirrors actual state-imposed conditions as served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-order rights and avenues for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.57(a) and 35 U.S.C. § 32, the practitioner may seek review of the final USPTO Director decision by filing a petition in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within thirty days of the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides procedural guidance on judicial review: time limit (30 days) and forum (E.D. Va.) and references local civil rules (E.D. Va. Local Civil Rule 83.5). The Director's order also directs publication and notifications per disciplinary rules.
